routes.name: Bear Harbor & Eel River Railroad
routes.path_source: Project's fixed waypoints (pier, incline base/top, Anderson/Indian confluence, Moody, Andersonia) densified with USGS NHD large-scale flowlines (hydro.nationalmap.gov nhd MapServer layer 6): GNIS 'Anderson Creek' incline top to confluence, GNIS 'Indian Creek' confluence to its named upstream limit near -123.831; coastal terrace leg (pier to incline base) and the final ~2 km of lower Indian Creek canyon into Andersonia hand-traced
sources: Carranco & Labbe, Logging the Redwoods (Caxton, 1975), Bear Harbor Lumber Co. chapter
California State Parks, Sinkyone Wilderness SP interpretive materials on the Bear Harbor grade and incline
Project research waypoints supplied with task (pier, incline, Moody, Andersonia)
routes.notes: 26.5 km total. Coastal terrace leg reconstructed along the shore bench; the gravity incline is drawn as the straight segment [39.9378,-123.9502] to [39.94286,-123.94783], which is faithful to an incline. NHD Anderson Creek's named headwater reach begins essentially at the incline-top waypoint (0 m snap), and the Indian Creek flowline passes 11 m from the fixed Moody waypoint, both strong validations. Rails ran on benches above the creeks; creek centerline is a corridor, not the grade.

routes.name: California Western Railroad (Fort Bragg-Willits)
routes.path_source: OSM via Overpass API: 78 ways tagged name='California Western Railroad' (railway=rail and railway=disused, operator Sierra Northern Railway) in bbox 39.30..39.48, -123.83..-123.33, stitched Fort Bragg depot to Willits by shortest-path over the way graph; 970 raw vertices simplified to 95; stitched length 63.1 km, consistent with the line's famous 40 miles
sources: Spencer Crump, Redwoods, Iron Horses, and the Pacific: The Story of the California Western Skunk Railroad (Trans-Anglo, 1963)
Active heritage operation (Skunk Train), Fort Bragg; line opened to Willits 1911 on the 1885-1905 Fort Bragg RR/CWR alignment
routes.notes: Real mapped geometry throughout: Fort Bragg, Pudding Creek, Tunnel 1 crossover into the Noyo watershed at [39.44846,-123.76426], the Noyo canyon, and the summit horseshoe loops west of Willits (the tight zigzags near -123.42 are genuine curves, not noise). Straight-looking chords are RDP simplification of tangent track.

routes.name: Caspar, South Fork & Eastern Railroad
routes.path_source: NHD flowline GNIS 'Caspar Creek' from the tidewater mill at Caspar anchorage upstream ~11 km, then a 1.9 km connector over the low divide (the straight step [39.37593,-123.71673] to [39.3876,-123.73232]), then NHD GNIS 'Hare Creek' upper flowline southeast to the camp country around -123.695
sources: Ted Wurm, Mallets on the Mendocino Coast: Caspar Lumber Company Railroads (Trans-Anglo, 1986)
Jackson State Forest interpretive record of Caspar Lumber Co. grades in the Caspar Creek and Hare Creek drainages
routes.notes: 18.1 km drawn. The divide connector into the Hare Creek watershed is conjectural in its exact crossing point; the creek corridors on either side are the sourced route. OSM contains one short way named 'Caspar Railroad' but it lies in the Albion River drainage 13 km south and was not used. The company also used the Jughandle Creek corridor for early logging; only the Caspar Creek main route is drawn.

routes.name: Mendocino Lumber Co. Railroad (Big River)
routes.path_source: NHD flowline GNIS 'Big River' from the tidewater mill and boom at the river mouth (Mendocino), followed upstream and trimmed at 13.5 km
sources: W. Francis Jackson, Big River Was Dammed (FMMC Books, 1991)
Carranco & Labbe, Logging the Redwoods (1975) on Mendocino Lumber Co. river and rail operations
routes.notes: Rails ran along the north bank above tidewater; the river centerline is used as the corridor. Terminus at ~8.5 miles is approximate because railheads and camps moved progressively upstream over the company's life; extend or trim to taste against the sourced end-of-track for your map's date.

routes.name: Albion & Southeastern / Albion River Railroad
routes.path_source: NHD flowlines GNIS 'Albion River' and 'South Fork Albion River' from the tidewater mill up the valley; a ~2.6 km conjectural divide crossing from the upper South Fork ([39.23762,-123.60649]) to the Flynn Creek headwaters; NHD GNIS 'Flynn Creek' down to the North Fork Navarro; NHD GNIS 'North Fork Navarro River' east; final ~2.6 km into Navarro (Wendling, [39.1546,-123.5372]) hand-bridged beyond the named flowline
sources: Fred A. Stindt & Guy L. Dunscomb, The Northwestern Pacific Railroad: Redwood Empire Route (1964), Albion branch (the A&SE was absorbed into the NWP system in 1907)
Carranco & Labbe, Logging the Redwoods (1975) on the Albion operations
routes.notes: 40.2 km drawn, consistent with the ~25-mile Albion-to-Wendling line as completed 1905. The Albion valley and Navarro valley segments are creek-corridor reconstructions; the divide crossing between the South Fork Albion and Flynn Creek is CONJECTURAL in its exact saddle and should be flagged on the map. The small wiggle at the Flynn headwaters is NHD branch geometry inside that conjectural zone.

routes.name: Glen Blair Redwood Co. Railroad
routes.path_source: Junction fixed from the OSM California Western geometry at the point where the mapped main line leaves Pudding Creek for Tunnel 1 (39.4485,-123.7643, verified within 77 m of the NHD creek line); branch then follows NHD GNIS 'Pudding Creek' flowline upstream for 5.2 km
sources: Spencer Crump, Redwoods, Iron Horses, and the Pacific (1963), Glen Blair Junction and the Glen Blair branch of the CWR
Mendocino County histories of the Glen Blair Redwood Co. mill on upper Pudding Creek
routes.notes: The junction point is solid (it is where today's mapped Skunk Train alignment turns away from Pudding Creek). The terminus is placed 5.2 km up the creek per the roughly 3-mile branch length in CWR accounts; I could not independently verify the Glen Blair townsite coordinates (gazetteer lookups failed this session), so treat the last kilometer as approximate.

routes.name: Usal Railroad
routes.path_source: NHD flowline GNIS 'Usal Creek' from the beach and wharf site at Usal cove, followed upstream and trimmed at 5.5 km (~3.4 mi)
sources: Carranco & Labbe, Logging the Redwoods (1975) on the Usal mill and railroad
Robert Dollar, Memoirs of Robert Dollar (1917 and later editions), his Usal operation of the 1890s
routes.notes: Wharf point at the creek mouth; the mill stood just upstream. Creek centerline used as the corridor for the roughly 3-mile line; terminus approximate.

routes.name: Crescent City & Smith River Railroad (Hobbs Wall)
routes.path_source: Wharf-to-town leg hand-traced NE from the Crescent City wharf; Elk Valley leg follows the NHD flowline GNIS 'Elk Creek' (Del Norte County) northeast through Elk Valley, trimmed near the mill site; OSM has no historic trace here (the only railway tags in the bbox are a modern boatyard marine railway)
sources: A. J. Bledsoe, History of Del Norte County, California (1881), early wharf and railroad of Hobbs, Wall & Co.'s predecessors
Del Norte County Historical Society materials on Hobbs, Wall & Co. and the Crescent City & Smith River Railroad
routes.notes: 6.4 km trunk drawn: wharf, through town, up Elk Valley to the mill area. The town leg is conjectural street-level routing. The NORTHERN BRANCH toward Lake Earl and Smith River (via Fort Dick) is NOT drawn because the schema takes one polyline per route; its corridor left the trunk near the north edge of town and ran roughly along today's Lake Earl Drive toward 41.845,-124.152 and on toward Smith River. Add it as a second feature if your build supports branches.

routes.name: Arcata & Mad River Railroad
routes.path_source: OSM via Overpass: abandoned/disused ways including one tagged 'Arcata and Mad River Railroad', the 'Annie & Mary Bridge', and connected 'Logging Railroad' ways, stitched Arcata to Korbel; one 3.4 km unmapped gap across the Arcata bottoms bridged straight ([40.87946,-124.08479] to [40.90501,-124.06917], the Warren Creek corridor); the bay wharf approach ([40.8412,-124.097] to Arcata) hand-added
sources: Stanley T. Borden's Western Railroader monograph on the Arcata & Mad River R.R.
Lynwood Carranco, Redwood Lumber Industry (Golden West, 1982); the 1854 Union Plank Walk predecessor and the Annie & Mary line
routes.notes: 20 km. Path verified to pass Glendale (40.903,-124.041), the Annie & Mary bridge site, and Blue Lake (40.884,-123.994) en route to Korbel on the North Fork Mad River. The wharf leg into Humboldt Bay is reconstructed (the historic Arcata wharf ran ~2 miles into the bay south of town); the straight bottoms gap should be flagged as bridged, not mapped.

routes.name: Humboldt Bay & Eel River Railroad / Pacific Lumber
routes.path_source: OSM via Overpass (kumi.systems mirror): NWP 'Humboldt Bay Block' ways (railway=rail/disused/abandoned), stitched Scotia to Fields Landing (35.7 km, one 1.1 km gap bridged near Alton) and Fields Landing to Bucksport (two gaps totaling 1.7 km bridged), trimmed at Bucksport
sources: Lynwood Carranco, Redwood Lumber Industry (1982), Pacific Lumber and the Humboldt Bay & Eel River lines
Stindt & Dunscomb, The Northwestern Pacific Railroad: Redwood Empire Route (1964); the HB&ER trackage became the NWP main
routes.notes: 42.3 km on the surviving NWP corridor, which directly overlies the 1880s-1900s HB&ER/Pacific Lumber route: Scotia mill, down the Eel past Alton (junction of the Carlotta branch, not drawn), through Fortuna and Loleta, around Table Bluff to Fields Landing (the original South Bay terminus), ending at Bucksport. About 2.8 km total of small mapped-data gaps are bridged straight.

routes.name: Dolbeer & Carson / Bucksport & Elk River Railroad
routes.path_source: Hand lead-in from Bucksport along the bay shore to the Elk River mouth; then NHD flowlines GNIS 'Elk River' (mainstem) and GNIS 'South Fork Elk River' to Falk at 40.6895,-124.1308 (Wikipedia article coordinates; the South Fork flowline passes 74 m from the townsite, the North Fork over 1 km, confirming the South Fork routing)
sources: Jon Humboldt Gates, Falk's Claim: The Life and Death of a Redwood Lumber Town (1983)
Lynwood Carranco, Redwood Lumber Industry (1982) on Dolbeer & Carson and the Elk River operations
Wikipedia, Falk, California (townsite coordinates 40.6895,-124.1308; the mill railroad extended five miles up the canyon in 1903)
routes.notes: 21.3 km including creek meanders. Today's BLM Elk River Trail into Headwaters Forest Reserve overlies the grade near Falk. The creek centerline stands in for the grade, which ran on the adjacent valley floor; the Bucksport shore lead-in is reconstructed.

routes.name: North Pacific Coast Railroad (Sausalito-Duncans Mills)
routes.path_source: Mostly OSM via Overpass: railway=abandoned ways over the NPC grade stitched in stages (Sausalito shore path, Alto tunnel corridor, old Corte Madera depot at Menke Park, Larkspur, Kentfield, Ross, San Anselmo, Fairfax, White's Hill, Lagunitas Creek/Cross Marin Trail, Tocaloma, Point Reyes Station, the Tomales Bay east shore, Keys Creek valley to Tomales, and on to Valley Ford); a 3 km unmapped gap through San Geronimo bridged; Valley Ford-Freestone-Occidental hand-traced on the road corridors that parallel the grade; Occidental to Monte Rio on NHD GNIS 'Dutch Bill Creek'; Monte Rio to Duncans Mills on NHD GNIS 'Russian River'
sources: A. Bray Dickinson, Narrow Gauge to the Redwoods: The Story of the North Pacific Coast Railroad (Trans-Anglo, 1967)
Modern rail-trail overlays of the grade: Mill Valley-Sausalito Path, Corte Madera Pathway, Cross Marin Trail (all tagged railway=abandoned in OSM)
routes.notes: 113.6 km, simplified hard to the 120-point cap with a step-length constraint so chords do not cut across Richardson or Tomales Bays. Documented (mapped abandoned grade) for roughly Sausalito-Valley Ford; the following are RECONSTRUCTED, flag if you symbolize by confidence: the San Geronimo gap ([38.0135,-122.6678] to [38.00989,-122.70198]), Valley Ford to Occidental (road-corridor points), and the Dutch Bill Creek and Russian River legs (creek geometry, grade ran beside them through Camp Meeker to Monte Rio and along the river's south side to Duncans Mills). The Sausalito start point is the ferry terminal; first mapped node is ~1 km north.

routes.name: Salt Point horse tramway
routes.path_source: Hand-drawn: no OSM trace, and NHD returned no feature named 'Miller Gulch' in the Salt Point bbox; straight terrace alignment from the Miller Gulch mill area to Gerstle Cove landing
sources: J. P. Munro-Fraser, History of Sonoma County (Alley, Bowen & Co., 1880), lumbering and chute landings at Salt Point
California State Parks, Salt Point SP interpretive materials on the Gerstle Cove landing
routes.notes: CONJECTURAL throughout, as permitted by the task. Endpoints: mill area placed at the gulch ~1.5 km NW of the cove, landing at Gerstle Cove. Draw dashed.

routes.name: Duncan's Landing horse tram
routes.path_source: Hand-drawn coast-parallel alignment on the marine terrace (today's Highway 1 bench) ending at Duncan's Landing cove (38.3927,-123.0947)
sources: A. Bray Dickinson, Narrow Gauge to the Redwoods (1967), the Duncan brothers' original coastal mill and the 1877 move upriver to Duncans Mills
Munro-Fraser, History of Sonoma County (1880)
routes.notes: ~1 mile per the project's research. The landing endpoint is firm (Duncan's Landing/Death Rock, Sonoma Coast SP); the mill endpoint is approximate, placed ~1 mile north on the terrace. If your sources place the mill at the Russian River mouth instead, extend the north end to ~38.435,-123.10 along the same terrace.

routes.name: Fort Bragg Railroad 1885 (pre-CWR logging line)
routes.path_source: OSM California Western Railroad geometry (same Overpass stitch as route 2), mill site to the point where the line leaves Pudding Creek at the later Glen Blair Junction/Tunnel 1 site
sources: Spencer Crump, Redwoods, Iron Horses, and the Pacific (1963): the Fort Bragg Railroad of 1885 ran from the mill up Pudding Creek and was reorganized as the California Western in 1905
routes.notes: NOT distinct trackage: the 1885 line's Pudding Creek alignment became the first miles of the CWR main and is still in service, so this path duplicates route 2's first 4.7 km deliberately. Its logging continuation up Pudding Creek beyond the junction is the corridor drawn as route 6 (Glen Blair). Recommended handling: fold this entry into route 2's notes rather than drawing a third overlapping line.

gaps: GEOMETRY VERIFICATION: every Overpass and NHD request used was confirmed to return geometry before use (way/feature counts and stitched lengths checked); stitched lengths cross-check historical mileages (CWR 63.1 km vs the famous 40 miles; Albion 40.2 km vs ~25 miles; A&MR passes Glendale/Blue Lake/Korbel; the fixed Moody waypoint sits 11 m off the Indian Creek flowline; Falk sits 74 m off the South Fork Elk flowline). REMAINING GAPS AND CAVEATS: (1) Glen Blair townsite coordinates could not be independently verified (Wikipedia 404, gazetteer mirrors failed, and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted); the branch terminus is placed 5.2 km up Pudding Creek per the ~3-mile branch length and should be checked against the USGS Fort Bragg 15-minute historic quad on TopoView before publication. (2) Hobbs Wall's northern branch toward Lake Earl/Fort Dick/Smith River is described in notes but not drawn (one polyline per route); no OSM trace exists in Del Norte. (3) TopoView historic-quad tracing was NOT performed this session; the 1916-1943 15-minute quads (Fort Bragg, Mendocino, Navarro, Crescent City, Fortuna, Arcata) are the best next step to upgrade the Caspar, Big River, Albion divide, Glen Blair, and Hobbs Wall reconstructions from creek-corridor to grade-accurate. (4) All NHD-based paths are creek centerlines standing in for grades that ran on adjacent benches; expect ~50-200 m lateral offset and extra meander wiggle. (5) Bridged straight gaps inside otherwise-mapped routes are identified in each route's notes (A&MR bottoms 3.4 km; NWP ~2.8 km total; NPC San Geronimo 3 km; Caspar divide 1.9 km; Albion divide 2.6 km) and should be symbolized as inferred if the map distinguishes. (6) Big River and Usal termini are era-dependent approximations (railheads advanced over time). (7) The Albion South-Fork-vs-mainstem choice above Christine and the exact divide saddle to Flynn Creek are the least certain parts of that route. (8) Salt Point is wholly conjectural; the Duncan's Landing mill endpoint is approximate with an alternative noted. (9) Calisphere was not consulted (bot-blocked per instructions); Bancroft/CSL photo collections and the county histories cited are the leads for further corroboration.
